questions.question: Obtain the Lagrange’s equation for angular motion in a central force problem. / [CO2]
questions.solution_html: • Classical Mechanics – Valuation Scheme October 2026 Angular momentum – 3 marks.The total angular momentum is L= ∑︂ i ri×pi, wherep i is the momentum of particlei. From rotational invariance and the Euler– Lagrange equations, dL dt = 0. Conclusion – 1 mark. L=constant . Thus, the total angular momentum of an isolated system is conserved due to the isotropy of space.

questions.solution_html:
• Classical Mechanics – Valuation Scheme October 2026 Physical significance – 2 marks.Galilean transformations preserve Newtonian me- chanics and use a common time coordinate. L= 1 √︄ 1− (0.8c)2 c2 m. Calculation – 1 mark. L= √ 1−0.64 m = √
  • 0.36 m. Final answer – 1 mark. L= 0.6 m .

questions.question: What was the ether hypothesis? / [CO4]
questions.solution_html:
• What was the ether hypothesis?
  • The ether hypothesis proposed that light waves require a medium called theetherfor
  • propagation. The ether was assumed to fill space and provide a reference frame in which
  • light propagated. Experiments such as Michelson–Morley failed to detect the expected
  • motion relative to the ether, challenging the hypothesis.Mark distribution:Definition
  • and explanation – 3.

questions.question: Explain simulataneity of events as a consequence of Lorentz transformation. / [CO4]
questions.solution_html: • ExplainsimultaneityofeventsasaconsequenceofLorentztransformation. The Lorentz time transformation is t′ =γ (︃ t− vxc2 )︃ , γ= 1√︂ 1−v 2/c2 . For two events, ∆t′ =γ (︄ ∆t− v∆xc2 )︄ . If∆t= 0, ∆t′ =−γ v∆xc2 . Thus, events simultaneous in one inertial frame are generally not simultaneous in another moving frame if they occur at different positions.Mark distribution:Interval relation – 1.5; explanation – 1.5.

questions.question: Differentiate between the special theory of relativity and the general theory of relativity. / [CO4] [3x10 = 30]
questions.solution_html:
• Differentiate between special and general relativity.
  • •Special relativity deals with inertial reference frames; general relativity extends the
  • description to gravity and accelerated frames.
  • •Special relativity describes spacetime without gravitational curvature in its standard
  • formulation; general relativity describes gravity through spacetime curvature.
  • •Special relativity explains time dilation and length contraction; general relativity also
  • explains gravitational time dilation and the bending of light by gravity.
  • Mark distribution:Any two valid comparative points – 1.5 marks each.

questions.question: Prove that the total angular momentum of the system is a constant using the idea of isotropy of space. / [CO1]
questions.solution_html:
• Prove that the total angular momentum of the system is a constant using
  • the idea of isotropy of space.
  • Isotropy of space – 2 marks.Isotropy means that the laws of physics remain un-
  • changed under rotations. The Lagrangian of an isolated system is invariant under an
  • infinitesimal rotation.
  • Infinitesimal rotation – 2 marks.For infinitesimal rotationδϕ,
  • δri =δϕ×r i.
  • Rotational invariance gives zero variation of the Lagrangian.

questions.solution_html: • ComparetheGalileanandLorentztransformations. Discusstheirphysical significance and explain the low-velocity limit. Galilean transformations – 2 marks. x′ =x−vt, y ′ =y, z ′ =z, t ′ =t. They assume absolute time and are used in classical mechanics. Lorentz transformations – 2 marks. x′ =γ(x−vt) , t′ =γ (︃ t− vxc2 )︃ , y′ =y, z ′ =z, γ= 1√︂ 1−v 2/c2 .
